INSIGHTS CORNER This presentation is non-exhaustive. For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Unlocking Biosimilars ֍What? ֍Why? ֍How? ֍When? of Biologic Alternatives

INSIGHTS CORNER This presentation is non-exhaustive. For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Introduction Biosimilars are biological medicines designed to closely match an already approved reference biologic in structure, function, and clinical performance. World Health Organization describes them as similar biotherapeutic products that require extensive comparison with the original medicine, and regulators like the US FDA require evidence showing no clinically meaningful differences in safety, purity, or potency FEATURE REGULATORY PATENTABILITY COST MARKET DIFFERENCE BETWEEN BIOLOGICS BIOSIMILAR BIOBETTER Original, innovator biological products that establish a new therapy (e.g., first monoclonal antibody for a target) Modified next-generation biologics designed to improve existing products (e.g., longer half-life, better efficacy, lower immunogenicity) Highly similar versions of an approved biologic with no clinically meaningful differences in safety, purity, or efficacy Assessed via full, standalone development program with comprehensive quality, non-clinical, & clinical data under standard biologics regulations Treated as new biologics, not eligible for the biosimilar pathway, and require full development to demonstrate improvements Abbreviated pathway demonstrating high similarity to the reference product through analytical, PK/PD, and limited clinical studies Being first-in-class or first-in-target allows them to have the most robust and lengthy patent protection Can build a new patent estate around the improved molecule, indications, and formulations, potentially securing stronger IP protection Biosimilar developers can patent specific processes or formulations, but these do not prevent others from developing different biosimilars Aim to introduce a new mechanism or standard of care and secure market exclusivity for as long as possible Aim to differentiate therapy with improved outcomes or convenience, targeting both switch patients and new starts rather than competing as a close copy Aim to compete with the reference biologic on price while maintaining comparable clinical performance, improving access and reducing healthcare costs Highest development cost and typically highest list prices at launch due to R&D recovery and limited competition Development costs are closer to innovator biologics & they are often premium-priced if they demonstrate clear clinical or practical advantages Developed at lower cost via an abbreviated pathway and typically priced below the reference product to support adoption and payer savings Bably

INSIGHTS CORNER This presentation is non-exhaustive. For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Biosimilars are important because they lower the cost of biologic therapies and make advanced treatments available to more patients and health systems 1 3 2 LOWER PRICES AND SYSTEM SAVINGS Biosimilars introduce competition for expensive brand-name biologics, which pushes down prices for both the biosimilars and the reference products. Studies in oncology, rheumatology, and other specialties show substantial reductions in total cost of care and drug spending when biosimilars are adopted, with multi-billion-dollar savings projected over time for health systems and payers. IMPROVED PATIENT ACCESS AND ADHERENCE Because biosimilars are typically priced lower than originator biologics, more patients can start or continue effective biologic treatment, especially in settings where cost was a major barrier. Increased affordability reduces treatment delays and medication abandonment, which supports better adherence and can prevent disease progression, particularly in low- and middle-income countries and underserved populations. BROADER HEALTH SYSTEM BENEFITS Savings from biosimilar use can be reinvested into other health priorities, such as funding more patients on biologics, expanding services, or adopting new innovations. As more biosimilars enter markets and policies encourage their use, competition is expected to keep biologic prices under pressure, contributing to long-term sustainability and more equitable access to high-cost therapies. Importance Bably

INSIGHTS CORNER This presentation is non-exhaustive. For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com EU REGULATORY PATHWAYUS REGULATORY PATHWAY REGULATORY AUTHORITY APPROVAL PATHWAY INTERCHANGEABILITY CLINICAL TRIAL EU pharmaceutical law (e.g., Directive 2001/83/EC) and EMA centralized procedure. EMA considers biosimilars scientifically interchangeable, but there is no formal EU “interchangeable” label & each member state sets its own switching and substitution rules. Comparative studies generally use an EU-authorized reference product Section 351(k) pathway of the public health service act “Interchangeable” designation allowing pharmacy substitution with additional switching evidence Comparative studies generally use a US-licensed reference product European Medicine Agency Food and Drug Administration Regulatory Pathway for Biosimilars US & EU Bably

INSIGHTS CORNER This presentation is non-exhaustive. For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Development Timeline: Biologics Vs. Biosimilars BIOLOGIC DEVELOPMENT TIMELINE DISCOVERY DEVELOPMENT PRECLINICAL PHASE I PHASE II PHASE III TRADITIONAL BIOSIMILAR DEVELOPMENT TIMELINE DEVELOPMENT PRECLINICAL PHASE I PHASE III RECENT STREAMLINED BIOSIMILAR DEVELOPMENT TIMELINE* DEVELOPMENT PRECLINICAL PHASE I 10-12 Years to develop and cost ~≥$1B 7-8 Years to develop and cost ~≥$100-300M 5-6 Years to develop and ~50% cost reduction Established Scientific Foundation: With the reference biologic’s mechanism of action, safety, and efficacy already validated, biosimilar developers primarily concentrate on proving high similarity instead of repeating the entire discovery process Abbreviated Regulatory & Clinical Development: Modern biosimilar regulations rely more on advanced analytical comparability and PK/PD studies, allowing smaller clinical programs and faster approvals Competitive Pricing & Improved Patient Access: Reduced development expenses allow biosimilars to enter the market at lower prices than originator biologics, supporting healthcare cost containment and broader patient access Moderate Price Reduction vs. Generics: Despite being cheaper than originator biologics, biosimilar price reductions are smaller than those seen with generics due to complex manufacturing and multi-year development timelines Bably *As per the US FDA’s draft guidance (proposed on Oct 29, 2025) aimed at eliminating unnecessary clinical testing

Denosumab biosimilars, with multiple approvals referencing PROLIA & XGEVA • 20 Denosumab biosimilars were approved in 2025 across the US (8) & EU (12), significantly increasing global market competition & biosimilar adoption • On Oct’25, FDA approved OMYLCO (omalizumab-igec), as the first & only interchangeable biosimilar to Xolair • As of Jul’25, US FDA approved Kristy (Insulin Aspart-xjhz), as the first & only interchangeable rapid-acting biosimilar with NovoLog (Insulin Aspart) • The US FDA is streamlining biosimilar development, were robust analytical, functional & PK data may reduce the need for comparative clinical efficacy (CES) or large-scale switching studies • Indian government is strengthening biosimilar regulations to align with global standards and ensure high-quality research & manufacturing as these therapies become key treatments for cancers & autoimmune diseases • WHO encouraging biosimilar adoption to improve access to biologics Therapeutics Portfolio Trends • The surge of biosimilars into oncology & autoimmune segments is expected to accelerate the future growth of US biosimilars market • Oncology biosimilars of HERCEPTIN, AVASTIN & RITUXAN are gaining market momentum due to high treatment expenses & reimbursement driven demand • Immunology biosimilars (for biologics such as HUMIRA, ENBREL, and REMICADE) are witnessing rapid adoption as an increasing number of alternatives enter the market • Expansion into diabetes (INSULIN biosimilars), ophthalmology (LUCENTIS, EYLEA biosimilars) & neurology (AIMOVIG, BOTOX biosimilars) is anticipated to significantly expand the market • Endocrinology Biosimilars of Denosumab (reference brands: PROLIA & XGEVA) are gaining momentum in the US and EU due to rising osteoporosis and oncology- related bone disorder burden, alongside strong cost- reduction and reimbursement-driven adoption Price Trends • Oncology ASPs declined across biosimilars, driven by price reductions and competitive discounts among key products • Supportive Care Mixed pricing trend-filgrastim biosimilars declined, while pegfilgrastim biosimilars increased • Immunology Mostly stable pricing, with a slight increase in infliximab biosimilars and a minor decline in tocilizumab biosimilars • Ophthalmology Highly stable pricing, with only a marginal decline in ranibizumab biosimilars Source: Samsung The therapeutic landscape for biosimilars is rapidly evolving, with immunology and oncology together representing majority share of FDA approvals • Regulatory: Since 2015's first biosimilar approval, the US FDA has developed a streamlined framework prioritizing swift market access • Regulatory guidance updates continue to refine requirements (e.g., potential reductions in human clinical studies required for approval of certain biosimilars and cut development costs) • Saving Impact: Biosimilars have saved the US healthcare system $56 billion to date. On average, ASP decreased by 52% within five years of the first biosimilar launch, with more mature markets achieving even greater price reductions over time (up to 77%). Countries such as China, India, and South Korea are emerging as major global hubs due to their cost-efficient research environments and skilled workforce • Regulatory harmonization Governments across Asia Pacific are strengthening regulatory frameworks for biosimilars to streamline approvals and ensure safety & efficacy. Harmonization of guidelines with global standards set by EMA & FDA further enhancing market confidence • Key Countries: o Significant investment in biotech firms with improved regulatory pathways through China NMPA, drive the growth of the biosimilars market o South Korea is a leader in biosimilar innovation, with companies such as Celltrion and Samsung Bioepis driving the growth of the country biosimilars market • Healthcare expansion Rising healthcare expenditures & insurance coverage in APAC are increasing demand for affordable biologic treatments, with biosimilars offering cost-effective alternatives for a growing patient population Nancy

INSIGHTS CORNER This presentation is non-exhaustive. For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com OPHTHALMOLOGY-ANTI-VEGF PIPELINE NEUROLOGY / MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS RARE DISEASE- COMPLEMENT-INHIBITOR GASTROENTEROLOGY/IMMUNOLOGY- VEDOLIZUMAB & NEXT-WAVE BIOSIMILARS • Ophthalmology (notably anti-VEGF therapies) is viewed by payers as a high-burden area where increasing biosimilar competition is expected to drive greater savings as more products launch over the coming years (2025-2030) • The pipeline includes several anti-VEGF biologics including high-dose Aflibercept (EYLEA HD), ophthalmic Bevacizumab-vikg (LYTENAVA), the antibody-biopolymer conjugate Tarcocimab tedromer (KSI-301) • Polpharma Biologics' TYRUKO (Natalizumab biosimilar) the first and only EMA- and FDA- approved MS biosimilar was developed entirely in- house and launched in the US in November 2025, demonstrating the feasibility of complex CNS biosimilar development and setting the stage for pipeline expansion into other MS biologics such as Ocrelizumab (PB018 in Polpharma pipeline) • New biosimilar programs are moving into very high-cost complement inhibitors, such as Samsung Bioepis’ EPYSQLI (Eculizumab), now approved in the US, EU and other markets as a SOLIRIS biosimilar for PNH and aHUS, with additional development toward gMG, positioning complement-inhibitor biosimilars to broaden access to rare-disease biologics and open a new rare-disease opportunity segment • Alvotech is conducting a P3 trial of AVT16 (Vedolizumab biosimilar) in moderate- to-severe ulcerative colitis, while Polpharma Biologics is advancing PB016, both targeting the ENTYVIO franchise with potential approvals expected around 2027+ • In January 2026, at the J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference, Samsung Bioepis announced six new biosimilar candidates (Dupilumab, Guselkumab, Ixekizumab, Vedolizumab, Ocrelizumab, and fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki) added to its pipeline expanding its early-stage programs across immunology, dermatology and oncology indications • Endocrinology particularly GLP-1 agonists and other metabolic agents, is flagged as an emerging “next wave” for biosimilars as these biologics become major cost drivers; TRULICITY (Dulaglutide) and related molecules are cited as strategic future biosimilar targets in the 2028–2030 period and beyond • Market analyses project continued growth in insulin biosimilar use through 2030, driven by pricing pressure and access needs, while Boan Biotech’s BA5101, a Dulaglutide biosimilar to TRULICITY has completed P3 in China and is under BLA review representing the first filed dulaglutide biosimilar globally ENDOCRINOLOGY- DIABETES/OBESITY Biosimilars are no longer confined to oncology and immunology; emerging therapy areas are reshaping the competitive landscape from 2026–2030 Market Trends in Emerging Therapy Area (4/4) Kriti PNH: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, aHUS: atypical Hemolytic uremic syndrome, gMG: generalized Myasthenia gravis

For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Market Entry Barriers Biosimilar adoption is constrained by a combination of regulatory, legal, commercial, manufacturing, and behavioral barriers that collectively delay market entry and limit competitive uptake Swathi Barrier Impact Severity Region Regulatory Complexity: Extensive comparability studies, clinical pharmacology programs, and immunogenicity data Development cost & timeline High Global Patent Thickets: Reference product manufacturers file numerous secondary patents on formulations, devices, manufacturing processes, and dosing regimens beyond the core molecule patent. Eg. 250+ patents for Adalimumab, 100+ for etanercept Market entry timing High Global Rebate Walls: Originator manufactures offer conditional rebates of 50–70% to PBMs contingent on exclusive or preferred formulary status. Net price dynamics make competition on list price alone insufficient for access Formulary access High US Physician Inertia: Physicians often resist switching stable patients to biosimilars due to nocebo effects, concerns about immunogenicity, and lack of familiarity Market penetration Medium US Data Exclusivity: Regulatory data exclusivity (12 years in US, 8+2+1 in EU) prevents biosimilar manufacturers from referencing originator dossiers until expiry Earliest entry timing Medium US/EU Co-pay Accumulator Programs: PBMs increasingly use accumulator adjustment programs that prevent originator co-pay card values from counting toward patient deductibles Patient switching Medium US Patient Support Infrastructure: Building infrastructure for nurse education, injection training, adherence programs, financial assistance is expensive and lags originator capabilities Patient experience Low US Group Purchasing Organizations (GPO) Contracting hold long-term supply agreements with reference manufacturers Hospital channel access Medium US

This aims to cut costs/time, boost competition against high-cost biologics and increase market share 2010 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 2021 20222020 2023 2024 2025 Background: The Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act (BPCIA) created a pathway in the US for biosimilars, allowing lower-cost alternatives to expensive biologic drugs in specialty pharmacies. Initially, biosimilars gained traction as more approvals were granted. Later, stronger FDA guidelines improved interchangeability, making it easier to use them for disease treatments. Over time, biosimilars were used more widely for immune-related conditions, while FDA actions helped lower development costs, boosting competition and expanding their use in oncology and autoimmune therapies. Prashant How Biosimilars are Transforming Specialty Pharmacies

EU has faster biosimilar uptake than the US due to single-payer national health system, tenders, substitution policies, and lack of rebate-wall dynamics US Medicare Part B (Physician-Administered) Reimbursement for originators : ASP +6% of originator ASP Reimbursement for qualifying biosimilars (IRA provision through 2027): ASP +8% of the reference product's ASP Medicare Part D (Pharmacy-Dispensed) Rebate system historically favored branded biologics because PBMs could extract larger rebates from originators fighting for formulary placement. Biosimilar manufacturers have less rebate room. Recent reforms (IRA, rebate rule discussions) are slowly reshaping this Commercial Payers Adoption varies widely. Some payers mandate biosimilar use (step therapy or non-medical switching policies); others allow incumbency to persist due to existing rebate contracts with originator manufacturers Market access is dominated by complex network of PBMs, private insurers and Medicare system EU EU is widely regarded as the global leader in biosimilar adoption • Single-payer systems, mandatory price-linkage, tender competition, and no interchangeability switching- study requirement create a fundamentally more biosimilar-friendly environment • Reimbursement is a member state competency each with distinct pricing rules, procurement models, and physician incentive structures ✓ In France, biosimilar prices are set at 40% below the originator ✓ Italy mandates a 20% discount on originator prices ✓ Germany employs a regulated pricing policy, but differs in its reliance on retail-level tendering rather than a centralized tendering framework ✓ UK operates under an unregulated pricing policy with NHS setting caps for high-cost biosimilars while tenders drive competition via flexible discounts ASP: Average Sales Price; WAC: Wholesale Acquisition Cost; PBM: Pharmacy Benefit Managers; CMS: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services; IDNs: Integrated Delivery Networks; GPOs: Group Purchasing Organizations Swathi

For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com US Case Study: Humira Biosimilar Adoption Challenges The 2023 adalimumab biosimilar launches exemplified PBM rebate traps blocking uptake, but 2024-2025 shifts toward biosimilar favouritism accelerated market erosion for Humira Initial Launch Barriers: • Nine adalimumab biosimilars entered the US in January 2023 at list price (WAC) discounts of 55-85% versus Humira, yet captured only <2% market share in one year • PBMs (Express Scripts, CVS Caremark, OptumRx) retained Humira as exclusive preferred on national commercial formularies due to high rebates PBM Strategic Pivot • External pressures from employers, policymakers, and the public over the lack of transparency and misaligned incentives in the rebate system prompted 2024 formulary overhauls • CVS Caremark excluded Humira from its 2024 national commercial formularies, favoring its Cordavis private-label biosimilar (Sandoz- manufactured, ~85% off Humira WAC). This was followed by Express Scripts and OptumRx causing Humira’s dominant market share to plummet almost overnight For 2025, Humira almost vanished from PBMs’ standard formularies. Swathi Source: Drugchannels.net

INSIGHTS CORNER This presentation is non-exhaustive. For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Swathi Production and Developmental Hurdles Cell Line & Expression System Biosimilar production must replicate innovator molecules, with challenges in glycosylation, clonal stability, and analytical comparability Process Sensitivity Changes to biomanufacturing steps such as a different vector, cell screening system, culture media, production or purification method, or excipients can impact a product’s safety and efficacy Scale-Up Complexity What works at lab scale often doesn't translate linearly to commercial-scale bioreactors, requiring re-optimization Purification & Formulation Designing chromatographic purification is challenging due to lack of standardization Raw Material Variability Complex biological raw materials vary lot-to-lot, adding another layer of variability to control Manufacturing Developmental Clinical & Regulatory Pathway Regulators may require PK/PD and efficacy studies depending on molecule complexity, increasing development cost and time. Lack of a harmonized global regulatory framework further complicates multi-market approvals Functional Assays Links structural similarity to clinical performance; developing sensitive, reproducible bioassays for complex biologics is technically challenging Extensive Characterization Burden Regulators require detailed analytical comparison of biosimilars and reference products across key structural and functional attributes, including sequence, structure, activity, purity, and impurities Immunogenicity Risk Minor structural or formulation differences can trigger unwanted immune responses that affects safety and efficacy Intellectual Property Landscape Originator companies filing secondary patents covering formulations, dosing regimens, and manufacturing processes to delay competition years beyond the expiration of the primary patent

Newer tech boosts 50% reductions in emerging markets Implications • From 2025-2034, 118 biologics face patent expiry, unlocking a $232-234B market for biosimilars • Attractive for investors with focus on high-margin, complex pipelines and China/global expansion • Biosimilar 2.0 represents a scalable, technology-powered growth frontier that delivers affordability, broader patient access, and strong commercial upside for strategic investors Background: Biosimilar 2.0 is transforming the market through advanced technologies like next-gen sequencing and AI-driven bioprocessing, enabling high-quality biosimilars for complex therapies. Global regulatory harmonization and patient-focused evidence boost confidence and safety. With strong growth in oncology and immunology, led by markets like China, combined with cost reductions from pricing competition and CDMO efficiencies, Biosimilar 2.0 offers significant market expansion and attractive investment opportunities Prashant

INSIGHTS CORNER This presentation is non-exhaustive. For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com These post and tweet counts are based on the presence of the keywords: "biosimilar," "biosimilars," #biosimilar, or #biosimilars. LinkedIn: • Spike in posts on denosumab (PROLIA/XGEVA) biosimilar approvals and EMA reflection paper • Heavy Q3 earnings digestion for Sandoz, Samsung Bioepis and other biosimilar leaders • “Banner year” 2025 recap with 20+ FDA biosimilar approvals and 2026 outlook • Peak chatter around JPM with CEOs selling the “Golden Decade” and interchangeability wins Twitter: • Peak buzz: Denosumab biosimilar approvals plus EMA clinical trial reflection paper • Strong focus on MENA build-out, especially Hikma-Celltrion moves • Continuous IRA / Medicare Negotiation threads tied to biosimilar pricing strategy • Year-end threads on record 18+ FDA biosimilar approvals in 2025 • #JPM26 live-tweets on the “Golden Decade” narrative and 2026 pipeline trackers Sentimental Analysis Ruchi Google Trends Based on Worldwide Web Search 8,500 7,000 6,500 5,500 10,000 8,500 7,500 4,500 4,000 3,500 8,000 5,500 Sep-25 Oct-25 Nov-25 Dec-25 Jan-26 Feb-26 Estimated Posts on LinkedIn Estimated TweetsPosts/ Tweets in last 6 months 0 20 40 60 80 100 120 Bevacizumab Trastuzumab Rituximab Pertuzumab The oncology biosimilar landscape shifted from market establishment to aggressive disruption during this six-month window. While established molecules like Trastuzumab, Bevacizumab, and Rituximab reached a mature "utility" phase - maintaining high search volume driven by 50–70% price discounts - Pertuzumab emerged as the primary trend-breaker. The Nov’25 FDA approval of POHERDY (the first interchangeable Pertuzumab biosimilar) triggered a massive search spike, signaling a new era of "auto-substitution" in breast cancer care. This was amplified by an October 2025 FDA draft guidance that streamlined the path to interchangeability by reducing the need for costly switching studies. By Jan’26, the focus at JPM shifted toward the "Next Wave," with companies like Biocon and Samsung Bioepis unveiling pipelines for PD-1 inhibitors (Nivolumab and Pembrolizumab). Overall, the period was defined by a transition from simply asking "What is a biosimilar?" to operationalizing interchangeability and high-value oncology pipelines.

INSIGHTS CORNER This presentation is non-exhaustive. For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Richard Saynor CEO of Sandoz, a global leader in generic and biosimilar medicines. He has led the company since 2019 and brings over 20 years of pharmaceutical industry experience across generics, biosimilars, and established medicines. KOL Analysis 1. Key Voice & Leadership Positioning: The posts from Richard Saynor, CEO of Sandoz, his messaging consistently highlights the future of affordable medicines and expanding patient access, aligning Sandoz with healthcare sustainability and innovation 2. Core Messaging Themes: The social media content emphasizes three major themes: o Access to Affordable Medicines Posts stress that biosimilars can significantly expand patient access to life- changing treatments, particularly for diseases such as cancer, rheumatoid arthritis, and Crohn’s disease o Market Opportunity for Biosimilars Saynor highlights that biosimilars currently represent less than ~7% of the global biologics market, signaling a major growth opportunity over the next decade o Policy & Regulatory Advocacy The content supports regulatory reforms, such as reducing unnecessary clinical trials and improving patent frameworks to accelerate biosimilar adoption 3. Strategic Narrative: The narrative presented across posts is that the next decade will be pivotal for biosimilars. With many biologics losing patent protection, biosimilars can drive: o Healthcare cost savings o Expanded treatment access o Reinvestment into innovation This positions Sandoz as ready to lead the next wave of affordable biologics globally. 4. Engagement & Audience Interaction: Audience engagement appears supportive and aligned with the message. Comments from industry professionals reinforce the view that: o Biosimilars are safe and effective alternatives o The current market penetration is still too low o Greater adoption is necessary to maximize healthcare system benefits 5. Brand & Reputation Impact: The social media activity strengthens Sandoz’s reputation in two ways: o Industry leadership in biosimilars o Advocacy for healthcare affordability Bably

For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Historical Overview • Before 21st century, China drug industry was dominated by traditional medicines, imports & low-cost generics. Then, about a decade ago, government began a coordinated effort to drive pharmaceutical innovation for the development of NCEs, antibodies, ADCs, vaccines, personalized medicines, etc. • The 11th (2006–2010) and 12th (2011–2015) FYPs aimed to improve the QoL for Chinese citizens by strengthening environmental protection & social welfare, with a focus on promoting domestic innovation rather than global engagement. Subsequently, the 12th and 13th FYPs shifted their focus toward advancing China’s biotechnology innovation on a global scale, targeting collaboration and competitiveness in markets such as US & EU • Over the next 5 yrs, 13th FYP (2016-2020) expands on the12th FYP, focus on innovation & continues the 11th FYP efforts to improve QoL through environmental, health, education, & social welfare initiatives • Innovation: Innovation is pillar to China 13th FYP, aimed at upgrading manufacturing, boosting global competitiveness including US & EU, and strengthening technological leadership • Coordinated development: Chinese government aims to strengthen regional inter-governmental coordination of policies, resources & urban planning through urbanization • Openness: 13th FYP aims to expand exports & targeted imports, boost inbound and outbound investment, promote international use of RMB, & strengthen China role in global economic governance • In 2017, China NMPA joined the ICH as eighth regulatory member, NMPA plans to speed up foreign drug entry into Chinese market and export of Chinese drugs to the ROW while supporting global competitiveness • In June 2018, China NMPA was elected to the ICH Management Committee, allowing China to continue its involvement in international drug development & registration • China out-licensing deals increased from 15 in 2019 to 33 in 2023, with oncology representing greatest share, nearly 4x rise from 7 out-licensing deals in 2019 to 27 in 2023 • In the next 6 yrs, 14th FYP (2021–2025) for foreign capital utilization indicates that China will further open up to foreign investment by reducing the negative list & simplifying regulations for foreign-funded enterprises, major initiatives of this plan includes:- • Further reduce the negative list that restricts foreign investment • Expand access for foreign investors in the healthcare • Promote greater foreign investment in R&D, new materials, biomedicine, and related sectors • Strengthen IP protections & ensure foreign companies have equal access to government procurement & project bidding • In 2019, WuXi Biologics, first Chinese biologics maker, received EMA GMP certification for producing TROGARZO (Ibalizumab-uiyk). The company also highlights its world-class facilities that allow simultaneous development & registration of innovative biologics & biosimilars for both China and international markets, including US and EU • In 2020, China’s first independently developed Trastuzumab for HER2-positive breast cancer got approval in both China (HANQUYOU) and the EU (ZERCEPAC) marking a milestone in the internationalization of Chinese biosimilars 2016-2018 2019-2021 To be continued…. For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com US & EU Policy Headwinds BIOSECURE Act: • Purpose: Restricts foreign companies especially from China, to access US genomic data via biotech • Key Restrictions: Prohibits procurement, grants, or contracts involving BCC (biotechnology companies of concern) • BCC criteria: Foreign-controlled biotech firms risking US data security • Implementation: Enacted on Dec 18, 2025, includes 5-year phase-out for pre-existing contracts on OMB’s BCC list Possible Retaliation from China: • China may impose export restrictions on a limited set of pharmaceutical products to increase pressure on Western companies • Blacklisting a U.S. pharmaceutical company that has minimal operations in China, as opposed to one that China’s healthcare industry relies on EU International Procurement Instrument (IPI) Measures: The EU Commission is blocking Chinese medical device firms from public tenders due to unequal market access and fairness concerns Retaliation from China: China also blocked medical device imports from other countries if EU-made components exceed 50% of the contract value China Expansion Policies Health China 2030 Promotes China as a global health leader by sharing prevention models and technologies, shaping governance, and expanding health industry markets 15th five- year plan Health Silk Road Promotes global health cooperation, infrastructure, and supplies while advancing China’s medical and biotech influence Background: • Rising policy headwinds: US and EU measures (BIOSECURE Act, IPI) are restricting Chinese biotech and medical device firms’ access to procurement, data, and contracts on security and fairness grounds • China’s response: China has initiated selective retaliation, including limits on medical device imports and potential use of export controls or blacklisting mechanisms • Strategic long-term push: Through Healthy China 2030, the 15th Five-Year Plan, and the Health Silk Road, China continues to promote biotech innovation, high-end manufacturing, and global health cooperation to expand international influence Emphasizes innovation-led growth, industrial upgrades, self- reliance, openness, and competitive opportunities for foreign businesses China Navigates Biotech Headwinds

For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Last 5 years of US - China pharma dealmaking 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 10 Chinese biotech and pharma companies are increasingly out-licensing internationally to access global markets, secure capital amid domestic funding pressure, and validate rapid innovation, especially in oncology and ADCs Since 2020, numerous out-licensing deals to the US and EU have spanned multiple therapy areas, though oncology remains the dominant focus with rising interest in immunology and metabolic disorders China’s ability to generate new drug candidates and advanced modalities (e.g., cancer therapies) is drawing global pharma majors that seek to diversify pipelines and future-proof their portfolios Over the past two years, out-licensing has clearly expanded beyond oncology into immunology, metabolic disorders, and other areas, showing China can now drive innovation across multiple therapeutic segments Deal-making peaked in 2021, then normalized in 2022–2023 and started to recover in 2024, suggesting a more stable post-COVID partnering environment for Chinese companies D&C licensing structures dominate, reflecting shift away from pure service/CDMO work toward innovation-driven, asset-based partnerships from discovery through to approved products, with roughly 30% of deals still at early stages Antibody-based oncology assets remain the core pillar, but technology is diversifying into ADCs, cell and gene therapy, RNA-based approaches, AI/ML-enabled platforms, and new indications such as obesity Both out & in-licensing volumes have declined since 2021; however, out-licensing now consistently matches or slightly exceeds in-licensing (about -23% vs -26%), marking China’s transition from technology importer to exporter Chinese companies increasingly seek worldwide rights instead of China-only territories, reinforcing their global ambitions while preserving oncology as their primary strategic focus Overall, China’s biopharma sector is evolving toward broader, more sophisticated global partnerships, combining diversified modalities, multi-therapy innovation, and a stronger emphasis on exporting homegrown assets Deal Insights

For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com How ASH’25 is reshaping Multiple Myeloma care?? 1 5 3 2 4 Practice-changing trial data in multiple myeloma, especially MAJESTEC-3 and other key studies, showed major survival and disease-control benefits. Powerful immunotherapies (bispecific antibodies, CAR T, tri-specifics) are moving earlier in treatment, not just for end-stage disease. Minimal residual disease (MRD) negativity is being cemented as a main treatment goal and guide for response-adapted therapy. New combinations (for example, teclistamab plus daratumumab) delivered unprecedented depth of response in early relapse, likely changing second-line standards. Emerging in vivo CAR-T and off-the-shelf antibodies promise wider access, shorter treatment duration, and potential treatment-free periods for some patients.

For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Teclistamab + Daratumumab About Teclistamab Teclistamab is a ready-to-use BCMA×CD3 bispecific antibody for multiple myeloma that redirects T cells to kill myeloma cells. • It delivers deep and durable responses with a manageable safety profile and offering an effective, accessible alternative to CAR-T therapy, including in earlier relapses • Teclistamab is already received accelerated approval from USFDA for r/r MM and marketed by Janssen (J&J) under the brand name TECVAYLI Key Outcomes Safety ✓ Phase 3 MajesTEC-3 trial (NCT05083169) (587 r/r MM pts., 1–3 prior lines) shows Tec-Dara greatly improves PFS and OS vs standard DPd/DVd, with mPFS not reached vs 18.1 mos and higher ≥CR and MRD-negative rates ✓ Safety profiles are broadly comparable between arms (similar grade 3/4 and grade 5 TEAEs), though infections are more frequent with Tec + Dara but considered manageable, leading to low treatment discontinuation due to adverse events ✓ Overall, Tec + Dara emerges as a highly effective, off-the-shelf immunotherapy that can serve as a new standard of care for r/r MM as early as first relapse Inclusion Criteria • 1–3 prior lines of therapy (LOT) • If 1 prior LOT → lenalidomide-refractory Exclusion Criteria • Prior BCMA-directed therapy • Refractory to anti-CD38 therapy • Prior anti-CD38 exposure allowed Endpoints & Assessments • 1EP: PFS by IRC • 2EP: ORR, >CR, OS, Safety & tolerability Study Design Randomization (1:1) Pts in r/r MM (N=587) Teclistamab (Tec) + Daratumumab (Dara) n=291 SOC Control arm (DPd/DVd) n=296 Efficacy Endpoints Tec + Dara (n=291) SOC (DPd/ DVd) (n=296) mPFS (mos) NR 18.1 36 mos. PFS rate (%) 83.4 29.7 ORR (%) 89.0 75.3 >CR rates (%) 81.8 32.1 36 mos. OS rate (%) 83.3 65.0 MRD-negativity (%) 58.4 17.1 Endpoints Tec + Dara (n=283) SOC (DPd/ DVd) (n=290) Pts. Remained on study (%) 71 28.3 mTD (mos) 32.4 16.1 Incidence of grade 3/4 (%) 95.1 96.6 Grade 5 TEAEs (%) 7.8 6.2 Treatment discontinued due to TEAEs (%) 4.6 5.5 Any grade infection (%) 96.5 84.1 Abb.: r/r MM: relapsed/ refractory multiple myeloma; mPFS: median progression-free survival; OS: overall survival; CR: complete response; MRD: minimal residual disease; TEAEs: treatment-emergent adverse events; IRC: Independent Review Committee; ORR: overall response rate; mTD: median treatment duration I Sources: ASH 2025_LBA-6 Median follow-up: 34.5 mos

For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Ramantamig About Ramantamig Ramantamig (JNJ-5322) is a next- generation tri-specific T-cell–engaging antibody that binds BCMA X GPRC5D (on myeloma cells) X CD3 (on T cells), designed to overcome tumor heterogeneity in r/r MM. Key Outcomes Study Design Pts in r/r MM Phase 1 Part 1 • Dose Escalation • Identify RP2D & Schedules Part 2 • Dose Expansion • Patients treated at RP2D • RP2D was identified as 100mg SC Q4W, following a single 5 mg subcutaneous step-up dose • Present updated safety results (N=36; mFU= 17.0 mos) and efficacy results in triple-class exposed patients naive to T-cell redirecting therapy (N=27; mFU=17.8 mos) at the RP2D from the ongoing phase 1 study. DCO: Sep’25 Efficacy At the RP2D, triple- class–exposed pts who were naive to T-cell - redirecting therapies achieved an ORR of 100.0% (n=27/27) , with responses further deepening since the prior analysis. Safety At the RP2D remained consistent with prior findings, CRS 53% of pts Grade 1: 42% Grade 2: 11% Incl. those who received prophylactic tocilizumab Safety (N=36) % of total TEAEs Any grade Grade ¾ Hematologic >10 Lymphopenia 47.2 44.4 Neutropenia 44.4 33.3 Non-Hematologic >30 Infections 77.8 33.3 Skin (non-rash) 66.7 0.0 Abb.: r/r MM: relapsed/ refractory multiple myeloma; RP2D: recommended Phase 2 Dose; SC: subcutaneous; Q4W: every 4 week; mFU: median follow-up; DCO: date cut-off; ORR: overall response rate; CR: complete response; MRD: minimal residual disease; CRS: cytokine release syndrome; ICANS: immune effector cell–associated neurotoxicity syndrome; SUD: step-up dose I Sources: ASH 2025_PN-4042 At the RP2D: ORR of 86.1% (n=31/36), ≥CR rate of 75.0%, and MRD-negativity rate of 100.0% at 10 –5 (n=10/10) and 10 –6 (n=7/7) ✓ The redesigned GPRC5D and CD3 binding domains, together with a single SUD and fixed Q4W dosing, likely contribute to this favorable safety profile, allowing convenient single step-up outpatient dosing and no grade ≥2 CRS or grade 3 oral events ✓ At the RP2D, ramantamig achieves a 100% overall response rate with deepening responses over time, including ≥CR in 88.9% of triple-class–exposed, T-cell–redirecting-therapy– naïve patients, and maintains robust, durable responses with high MRD negativity ✓ At the fixed RP2D of 100 mg Q4W, ramantamig (JNJ-5322) shows a favorable safety profile Vs. BCMA/GPRC5D bispecific antibodies, with low oral adverse events, minimal weight loss, low CRS rates, no ICANS, and manageable infections using optimized infection-management strategies

This CAR enables T cells to recognize a specific target antigen on diseased cells with high precision. Key Outcomes About Anitocabtagene Autoleucel ✓ Efficacy is robust, with PFS rates of 82.1% and OS of 94% at 12 mos ✓ Safety shows mainly low-grade CRS and manageable hematologic AEs, positioning it as an advanced precision immunotherapy with potent, selective activity ✓ These results supports anito-cel for a potential U.S. launch in 2026 Abb.: r/r MM: relapsed/ refractory multiple myeloma; mFU: median follow-up; DCO: date cut-off; mPFS: median progression-free survival; mOS: median overall survival; MRD: minimal residual disease; CR: complete response; mT1mos: median time 1 month; CRS: cytokine release syndrome; AEs: adverse effect I Sources: ASH 2025_PN-256; Gilead PR Dec’25 I Data captured based on press release, which has a later data cutoff (Oct’25) than ASH abstract (May’25), so it reflects the most recent results.

INSIGHTS CORNER OCTAVUS∞ CONSULTING GLP - 1 and GIP “Small Signals. Big Impact on Metabolism”

INSIGHTS CORNER OCTAVUS∞ CONSULTING GLP-1 vs GIP❑ Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) agonists are a class of medications utilized to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), Obesity and Others INTRODUCTION Illustration demonstrating the secretion and effects of GLP-1 and GIP peptides on various organs ➢ GLP-1 (Glucagon- Like Peptide-1): incretin hormone that plays a crucial role in glucose metabolism ➢ GIP (Glucose-Dependent Insulinotropic Polypeptide): another incretin hormone that enhances insulin secretion in response to nutrient intake ➢ GLP-1 medications enhancing insulin secretion and reducing glucagon levels, thereby lowering blood glucose levels ➢ Whereas GIP medications focus on stimulating insulin release in response to meals and have a more pronounced effect on lipid metabolism GLP-1 Cardiac Output Cardio Protection GIP No Prominent Effect GIP Fat Accumulation GLP-1 Gastric Emptying GIP Gastric Acid SecretionGLP-1 No Prominent Effect GIP Bone Remodelling GLP-1 Glucose Uptake GLP-1 Insulin Glucagon GIP Insulin, Glucagon GLP-1 Memory Food Intake GIP Memory GLP-1 & GIP BRAIN PANCREAS MUSCLES BONES GI TRACT ADIPOSE TISSUE HEART FDA-Approved GLP-1/GIP Medications zepbound logo - Austin Thyroid and Endocrinology

It highlights PD-1/PD-L1 agents like pembrolizumab and GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, dulaglutide, liraglutide) plus tirzepatide as priority treatments, while urging countries to use fair pricing, promote generic competition, and strengthen primary care so these high-impact medicines become widely accessible, especially in low- and middle-income settings. INSIGHTS CORNER OCTAVUS∞ CONSULTING ADVANCEMENTS AND MILESTONES Innovent Biologics: Mazdutide (GLP-1/ GCG dual receptor agonist) Innovent Biologics announced that the CDE of China’s NMPA acceptance of supplementary application of 9 mg dosage of mazdutide (GLP-1/ GCG) for review for moderate-to-severe obesity, based on the P3 GLORY-2 registrational study results Results Analysis: • P3 GLORY-2 registrational study results evaluated efficacy and safety of mazdutide 9 mg vs PBO in Chinese adults for obesity, as it showed • Primary Endpoints: Mazdutide 9 mg group achieved a mean weight reduction of 18.55%, compared to 3.02% in the placebo group. 44.0% of participants in the mazdutide 9 mg group achieved a weight reduction of 20% or more, versus 2.6% in the placebo group • Secondary Endpoints: Mazdutide 9 mg led to a weight loss of 20.08% by Week 60 in non-diabetic participants, with nearly 48.7% losing over 20% of their weight, compared to 3.1% in the PBO group. The weight loss trend had not plateaued by the study's end • Furthermore, mazdutide 9 mg significantly led to substantial reduction in liver fat content, achieving a mean % decrease from the BL of 71.9%. Additionally, significant improvements in various cardiometabolic metrics, including BP, blood lipids, and serum uric acid levels, as well as a marked reduction in waist circumference • Safety: Mazdutide 9 mg showed favorable safety profile, with no new AEs Milestone: • Planning to present detailed results from P3 GLORY-2 registrational study at future international academic conferences or in scientific publications Novo Nordisk: Amycretin (GLP-1/Amylin receptors) Novo Nordisk released positive results from P2 study of Amycretin (GLP-1/ Amylin receptors) administered as once-weekly SC and Once- daily oral for T2D • P2 study evaluated efficacy, safety and PK of once-weekly SC and once-daily oral amycretin vs PBO for T2D inadequately controlled on metformin with or without SGLT2i as SoC Results analysis: • In once-weekly SC, at mean baseline HbA1c of 7.8%, -1.8% achieved dose-dependent reductions in HbA1c by week 36 and 89.1% and 76.2% of patients achieved HbA1c <7% and ≤6.5% respectively • In once-daily oral, at mean baseline HbA1c of 8.0%, -1.5% achieved dose-dependent improvements in HbA1c by week 36, 77.6% and 62.6% of patients achieved HbA1c level of <7% and ≤6.5% respectively • From a mean BL body weight of 99.2 kg, SC amycretin showed statistically significant weight loss of up to -14.5%, Whereas, from mean BL body weight of 101.1 kg, oral amycretin also showed statistically significant weight loss of up to -10.1% • Safety: Both SC and oral amycretin showed favorable and well-tolerated safety profile, consistent with other incretin and amylin-based therapies. • Most common AEs were gastrointestinal, and the vast majority were mild to moderate in severity Milestone: • Based on these results, planning to initiate P3 study development programme with amycretin for T2D in 2026

INSIGHTS CORNER OCTAVUS∞ CONSULTING MARKET TRENDS • The GLP-1 therapy market, dominated by agonists for type 2 diabetes and obesity • GLP-1 receptor agonists are being researched for uses beyond diabetes and obesity, like heart disease, fatty liver disease, and brain conditions, which will likely increase the market • Novo Nordisk has recently received approval for semaglutide in the treatment of MASH • Companies like Eli Lilly, Boehringer Ingelheim, Novo Nordisk, Amgen, Viking Therapeutics, Regor Therapeutics, Carmot Therapeutics, Roche, and others are developing novel GLP-1 agonists for upcoming market entry • About 11.8% of Americans have used GLP-1 drugs to lose weight, around 14% are interested, and 74% do not plan to use (according to RAND survey) • Women, particularly aged 30-64, use GLP-1 drugs much more than men, highlighting the need for gender-tailored messaging and benefits • The global GLP-1 receptor agonist market size was estimated at $53.5B in 2024 and is projected to reach $268.3B by 2034, growing at a CAGR of 20.10% from 2025 to 2034 • Eli Lilly's revenue rose 54% to $17.60 billion in Q3 2025, mainly driven by increased sales volume of its GLP-1 agonist products, MOUNJARO and ZEPBOUND • The GLP-1 agonist market is poised for growth next year, supported by Eli Lilly's investments in manufacturing capacity and oral candidates such as orforglipron • The global autoinjectors market is rapidly growing, with Ypsomed and Sidekick Health partner to launch a smart autoinjector platform for improved GLP-1 obesity treatment • Digital health platforms, like Hims & Hers, Ro, and WeightWatchers launched GLP-1 programs with prescriptions, coaching, and insurance help to meet Wegovy/Ozempic demand • In April 2025, Novo Nordisk teamed up with Hims & Hers for the first U.S. online direct sales of Wegovy via telehealth. INSIGHTS CORNER OCTAVUS∞ CONSULTING GLP-1-BASED THERAPEUTICS SUMMIT 2026 OCTAVUS INSIGHT ❑ Major players like Eli Lilly, AstraZeneca, and Sanofi are expanding GLP-1 pipelines into diverse indications beyond obesity and diabetes, such as MASH, MASLD, kidney disease, Alzheimer's, and Parkinson’s, underscoring the breadth of their development strategies and the expanding GLP-1 market ❑ New entrants like Canary Global, Fractyl Health, Constructive Bio, etc. are advancing GLP-1-related therapies, signaling strong industry-wide interest and highlighting GLP-1's strategic importance from both market and patient-need perspectives ❑ Targeted genetic therapies are emerging for GLP-1-based treatments, demonstrating that GLP-1 applications extend beyond specific patient populations to broader personalized care ❑ Ongoing research explores GLP-1 for addiction and substance use disorders, positioning it as a versatile platform far beyond endocrine diseases with vast therapeutic potential ❑ With GLP-1 research accelerating daily, now is an ideal time for companies to enter this dynamic market

INSIGHTS CORNER OCTAVUS∞ CONSULTING EXECUTIVE SUMMARY Market Opportunity: Incretin Hormones (GLP-1, GIP & Dual Agonists): A $268B Global Opportunity • Global GLP-1 market valued at $53.5B in 2024, projected to reach $268.3B by 2034 (20% CAGR) • Obesity prevalence expected to rise >115% from 524M (2010) to 1.13B adults by 2030 • Rapid expansion into obesity, T2D, MASH, CV protection, and CNS indications • Strong reimbursement momentum and digital-health enabled access accelerating adoption • High unmet need + powerful clinical outcomes = one of the fastest-growing therapeutic classes • Novo Nordisk is fueling market expansion by strategically cutting prices on its GLP-1 powerhouses Patent & Regulatory Landscape: • Multiple high-value patents expiring over next decade → opportunity for generics/biosimilars • Accelerated pathways for various therapeutics indication speeding approvals Investment Thesis: Why Investors Should Prioritize the Incretin Segment: • Massive Market Expansion: $50B → $268B within a decade • Extraordinary Efficacy: Best-in-class weight reduction and metabolic improvements • Pipeline Depth: Dual & tri-agonists poised to redefine standard of care • Strong Commercial Momentum: Lilly & Novo are setting historic revenue records • Durable Demand: Chronic conditions ensure long-term therapy needs • Multiple Entry Points: • Innovator pipelines • Digital-health partnerships • Autoinjector/smart device companies • Future biosimilar opportunities post-patent expiry Conclusion: Incretin therapeutics represent one of the strongest long-term growth opportunities in global biopharma, backed by robust science, expanding use-cases, and proven commercial demand

INSIGHTS CORNER OCTAVUS∞ CONSULTING EXECUTIVE SUMMARY Overview: • GLP-1 and GIP based therapies are significantly changing the management of obesity and T2D, presenting as largest, fastest-growing biopharma opportunity over the next decades, that is being driven by strong data outcome and expanding into various multiple indication such as MASH, CVD, CKD, OSA • Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly being the market leaders, whose GLP-1 and dual agonist drugs dominates both diabetes and obesity segment • The crowded late stage pipeline in single/ dual/ triple agonist along with oral and subcutaneous formulation and high value partnering and licensing deals shows intense competition and interest for the advancement in metabolic therapy area • With the recent FDA and WHO guidelines on GLP-1 for quality, compounding and essential-medicine status, highlights both the strategic importance of these drugs and the need for secure, compliant supply chains and risk management. • With the patent expiry from late 2030s onwards, open up the space for generic with low pricing and increasing market population

Worldwide adult obesity has more than doubled since 1990, and adolescent obesity has quadrupled. In 2022, 43% of adults aged 18 years and over were overweight and 16% were living with obesity. In 2024, 35 million children under the age of 5 were overweight . In 2022, 2.5 billion adults (18 years and older) were overweight. Of these, 890 million were living with obesity. Over 390 million children & adolescents aged 5–19 years were overweight in 2022, including 160 M who were living with obesity. ➢ Overweight is a condition of excessive fat deposits. It is a chronic complex disease defined by excessive fat deposits that can impair health. Individual with BMI over 30 is considered obese

INSIGHTS CORNER OCTAVUS∞ CONSULTING NOVO NORDISK @ ObesityWeek 2025 Title: Novo Nordisk's CagriSema associated with significant reduction in blood pressure and showed anti-inflammatory effects while reducing the proportion of patients at risk of developing heart disease over time in new analyses at ObesityWeek Summary: Presented post-hoc results of P3 REDEFINE1 study of CagriSema (2.4 mg/2.4 mg), that showed: • 0.9 mmHg reduction in systolic blood pressure, allowing 40% of people on blood pressure medications to reduce or stop their medication • ~70% of patients showed reduction in key inflammatory marker associated with increased cardiovascular risk • Also showed that fewer people on CagriSema were at intermediate-to-high risk of developing ASCVD within the next 10 years • Showed favourable safety results and results were published in Hypertension Title: Novo Nordisk presents four new analyses on oral semaglutide 25 mg (Wegovy in a pill) at ObesityWeek 2025, including demonstrated reductions in cardiovascular risk factors Summary: Presented results of P3 OASIS 4 study of semaglutide 25 mg vs PBO, that showed: • Participants treated with oral semaglutide 25 mg were more likely to achieve ≥15% body weight reduction • Within the semaglutide group, more people who achieved ≥15% body weight reduction saw larger improvements than those with <15% weight reduction in systolic (−10.1 mmHg vs −4.1 mmHg) and diastolic (−4.3 mmHg vs −1.1 mmHg) blood pressure • Showed reduction in levels of inflammatory marker C-reactive protein (0.34 vs 0.74) and in lipids (blood fats), including non–high density lipoprotein cholesterol (0.90 vs 0.96) and triglycerides (0.73 vs 0.87) Title: Novo Nordisk Wegovy users achieved waist and BMI targets linked to improved health and low risk of obesity-related complications Summary: Presented results of P3b STEP UP study of Wegovy, that showed: • BMI under 27 and a waist-to-height ratio of less than 0.53

item.title: Octavus Insights Corner - AACR (June 2025)
item.description: Octavus Insights Corner for June 2025: AACR.
item.content:encoded:
ABOUT US Octavus is a global business intelligence consulting, specialized in providing holistic market solutions for diverse Healthcare and Life sciences sector including Pharma, Biopharma, MedTech, Nutraceuticals, Cosmetics, Diagnostics, Digital health, Animal health, HealthTech and Healthcare start-ups

WHAT IS INSIGHTS CORNER INSIGHTS CORNER

INSIGHTS CORNER

AGENDA Objectives: • Highlight the most impactful scientific advances, novel therapies, and emerging technologies presented at AACR 2025 • Summarize key trends in cancer research, clinical trials, and drug development, including the role of artificial intelligence​ • Share actionable insights and future outlooks for oncology professionals and stakeholders​ Key Sections​ • Introduction & AACR 2025 Overview​ • Major Scientific Highlights & Breakthroughs​ • New Drugs, Clinical Trials & Technologies​ • Artificial Intelligence in Cancer Care​ • Trends, Future Outlook & Q&A​ Number of Abstract Sessions Sessions No. of Sessions No. of Presentations Clinical Trials Minisymposia 3 56 Clinical Trials Plenary Sessions 4 63 Clinical Trials Poster Sessions 9 171 Late-Breaking Minisymposium 1 9 Late-Breaking Poster Sessions 22 363 Minisymposia 37 397 Poster Sessions 276 6237 May 2025

AACR 2025 ANNUAL MEETING (25-30 APR) “Unifying Cancer Science and Medicine: A Continuum of Innovation for Impact” Proffered Abstracts Exhibitors Educational Sessions Major Symposia Plenary Sessions 7000+ 600+ 65 50 6

ABSTRACTS CATEGORY 1 Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Systems Biology, and Convergent Science 2 Chemistry 3 Clinical Research: Solid Tumors and Hematologic Malignancies 4 Clinical Trials: Solid Tumors and Hematologic Malignancies 5 Endocrinology 6 Experimental and Molecular Therapeutics 7 Immunology 8 Molecular/Cellular Biology and Genetics 9 Population Sciences 10 Prevention, Early Detection, and Interception 11 Regulatory Science and Policy 12 Science and Health Policy 13 Tumor Biology

DAY-1 26TH-APR First major scientific session, “Discovery Science Plenary: Novel Mechanisms Influencing Cancer Evolution” Over 65 Educational Sessions and Methods Workshops concluded The AACR Runners for Research 5K Run/Walk saw over 850 participants and raised more than $273,000 for cancer research Two key sessions addressed 1 2 3 4

DAY-2 27TH-APR The AACR announced its largest-ever grant initiative 1 Opening Plenary: Unifying Cancer Science and Medicine 2 Clinical Trials Program: Immunotherapy and Targeted Therapy Advances • KEYNOTE-689 Study: Pembrolizumab before and after surgery in HNSCC • dMMR Tumors: PD-1 • Combination Therapy: PD-1 immunotherapy with the PARP inhibitor (Olaparib) • Early data on a Werner helicase inhibitor for MSI/dMMR tumors 3 Two sessions unveiled eight novel therapeutic molecules, including: • New RAS pathway inhibitors (AMG 410, RMC-5127) • Immune-targeting agents (HER2 x CD3 engager, FAP- targeting drugs) • Androgen receptor and transcription factor inhibitors, among others 4 Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Cancer Research 5 Sessions explored the lifestyles impact on cancer risk 6

DAY-3 28TH-APR Plenary Session: Innovative Technologies Driving Cancer Research • Organoid Models • CAR T Cell Engineering • Liquid Biopsies • Decentralized Clinical Trials 1 Clinical Trials Plenary: New Therapies for Lung Cancer • HER2 Inhibitor Zongertinib • EGFR Inhibitor Aumolertinib • ROS1 Inhibitor JYP0322 • TIGIT Antibody Tiragolumab 2 New Drugs on the Horizon • BAY 3547926 • M0324 • AZD0022 • GSK4418959 (IDE275) 3 Advances in Liquid Biopsy • The VICTORI trial 4 Hematologic Malignancies: AML Atlas 5 Rare Tumors and AI 6

DAY-4 29TH-APR Plenary Session: Targeting the Cancer Ecosystem • Tumor Heterogeneity & Immunogenicity • Immune System Archetypes • Spatial Heterogeneity • Metastatic Evolution Special Session: Overcoming Hurdles in Therapeutic Translation • Using predictive biomarkers to select patients most likely to benefit or develop resistance. • Improving tumor sampling technologies to better capture heterogeneity. • Employing digital twins and virtual trials to model drug effects. • Emphasizing the value of learning from negative results and optimizing investment decisions in experimental drugs Clinical Trials Plenary: Biologics and T-cell Engagers • CD40 Agonist Antibody • HER2/CD3 Bispecific Antibody (Runimotamab) • Invikafusp Alfa • ICAM-1 CAR T-cell Therapy (AIC100) Advances in Cancer Vaccines • New approaches for identifying and targeting neoantigens • Personalized mRNA neoantigen vaccines • Novel delivery methods 1 2 3 4 Poster Sessions: Breast Cancer Mortality and Survivorship 5 Combined Liquid and Tissue Biopsy for Tailored Therapy • The phase II ROME trial demonstrated using both tissue and liquid biopsies 6 Developmental Origins of Childhood Cancer 7

NEW ONCOLOGY DRUGS REVEALED DRUGS MoA Indication AMG 410 pan-KRAS inhibitor CRC, PDAC, NSCLC GDC-2992 AR degrader Prostate cancer ABBV-969 Bispecific PSMA/STEAP1 antibody drug conjugate Prostate cancer ABP-102/CT-P72 HER2 x CD3 bispecific T cell engager Breast cancer, Gastric cancer BMS-986449 CELMoD molecular glue degrader of IKZF2/4 Solid Tumors RMC-5127 KRAS G12V RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor PDAC and NSCLC FXX489 FAP-targeting 177Lu radioligand PDAC, NSCLC, Breast and Colorectal cancer RO7567132 FAP x LTBR bispecific antibody Solid Tumors BAY 3547926 GCP3-targeted 225Ac-radioligand antibody Hepatocellular carcinoma GSK4418959 (IDE275) WRN helicase inhibitor CRC and Endometrial cancer AZD0022 KRAS G12D inhibitor CRC, PDAC and NSCLC M0324 MUC1/CD40 bispecific antibody Solid Tumors COMPANY

2025 NEXTGEN STARS Researchers recognized for their innovative cancer research Universities Cancer Research Topics Edmond Chan, MD Columbia University • Exploring dysregulated ribosomal homeostasis in 9p21.3 deleted cancers and microsatellite unstable cancers Yash Chhabra, PhD Fox Chase Cancer Center • Investigating age- and sex-differential changes in the tumor microenvironment to inhibit metastasis and enhance therapy responses in melanoma Karen O. Dixon, PhD University of Basel • Studying PI5P4K as a molecular checkpoint of anti-tumor immunity Adam D. Durbin, MD, PhD St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital • Developing a genome-derived non-coding reporter to dissect and control intratumoral heterogeneity and chemoresistance Anniina Farkkila, MD, PhD University of Helsinki • Mapping chemotherapy-induced myeloid-driven spatial exhaustion in ovarian cancer and targeting the NECTIN2-TIGIT interaction Anand D. Jeyasekharan, MBBS, PhD National University of Singapore • Investigating lymphoma cell spatial organization with MYC-BCL2 co-expression and its impact on immune microenvironment Zuzana Keckesova, PhD Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry • Exploring cancer-resistant tissues for novel tumor suppressor identification John R. Prensner, MD, PhD University of Michigan • Mapping the functional microproteome in cancer Elvin Wagenblast, PhD Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai • Studying developmental dependency and metabolic vulnerabilities in NUP98-rearranged pediatric leukemia Stephanie Z. Xie, PhD University Health Network • Investigating inflammatory memory and selective advantage in human clonal hematopoiesis Di Zhao, PhD MD Anderson Cancer Center • Decoding actionable tumor suppressor defects for personalized cancer medicine

ABP-102/CT-P72: PRECLINICAL DATA ABP-102/CT-P72, a tetravalent bispecific HER2 x CD3 T-cell engager ABP-102/CT-P72 is product from strategic partnership of Abpro and Celltrion for worldwide development and commercialization Key Findings Highly Selective Tumor Killing • ABP-102/CT-P72 effectively targets HER2-overexpressing breast and gastric cancers while minimizing impact on HER2-low cells, overcoming a major drawback of previous HER2-targeted T-cell engagers Enhanced Tumor Growth Inhibition • In vivo studies demonstrated ABP-102/CT-P72 achieved up to twice the tumor suppression of a runimotamab biosimilar, a leading HER2xCD3 bispecific antibody Reduced Cytokine Release • ABP-102/CT-P72’s monovalent CD3 binding reduces cytokine toxicity by lowering cytokine release in HER2-low environments while preserving strong tumor-killing effects in HER2-high cancers Improved Tolerability • Dose escalation studies in cynomolgus monkeys showed ABP-102/CT-P72 was well tolerated at 180 times the maximum tolerated dose of the parental antibody, indicating a broader therapeutic window • ABP-102/CT-P72’s strong safety and efficacy profile could make it a leading HER2-targeted therapy, expanding treatment options for HER2-positive cancers • The broader therapeutic window may allow higher dosing and better patient tolerance, increasing its market potential; trial initiation is expected in 1H’26 • Partnership with Celltrion supports faster development and global commercialization efforts • Positive preclinical data may boost investor confidence and put competitive pressure on existing HER2 therapies Implications

AIC100, a third generation ICAM-1 directed CAR T-cell product engineered with affinity-tuned technology to selectively bind and kill tumor cells to improve safety NCT04420754 AIC100 (at dose levels (DL) 1x 107, 1 x 108, and 5 x 108) (n= 15; Data cut-off date: 12 Dec 2024) AIC100: P-I DOSE-ESCALATION STUDY RESULTS DL1: AIC100 at 1x 107 DL2: AIC100 at 1x 108 DL3: AIC100 at 5x 108 DL4: AIC100 at 7.5x 108 DLTs 0 - ORR at day 42 after infusion (%) 0 22 - ORR for ATC pts (%) 0 50 - DCR at day 42 after infusion (%) 0 56 - DCR for PDTC pts (%) 0 60 - Study Design • AIC100 shows promising efficacy and safety in treating aggressive thyroid cancers, with affinity tuning enhancing tumor targeting while minimizing side effects • Its built-in DOTATATE PET imaging enables real-time treatment monitoring and early positive results support further development and potential expansion to other ICAM-1-expressing tumors Implications DL1: AIC100 at 1x 107 DL2: AIC100 at 1x 108 DL3: AIC100 at 5x 108 DL4: AIC100 at 7.5x 108 Grade 3 Pneumonitis 0 2 Grade 1/2 CRS 0 10 • Based on safety and efficacy, DL3: AIC100 at 5x 108 was declared as RP2D; Cohort expansion at RP2D for ATC and PDTC will be initiated in 2Q’2025 • 24 patients enrolled of which 15 (8 ATC; 7 PDTC) were infused with AIC100 at 4DLs • 1 Endpoint: Safety assessment/DLTs within 30 days of AIC100 infusion and recommended P-II dose (RP2D) P-I (N=24) (Newly diagnosed and R/R anaplastic thyroid cancer (ATC) and R/R poorly differentiated thyroid cancer (PDTC)) AIC100 at 1x 107 AIC100 at 5x 108 AIC100 at 1x 108 AIC100 at 7.5x 108

AUMOLERTINIB: P-III STUDY RESULTS Aumolertinib, a third generation selective EGFR-TKI AENEAS2 Aumolertinib (110 mg QD) +/- Chemotherapy (pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 + cisplatin 75 mg/m2 or carboplatin) (N= 624; Data cut-off date: 18 Jun 2024) Aumolertinib + Chemotherapy Aumolertinib mPFS (mos) 28.9 18.9 OS Immature with event-patient rate 21.6% Hazard Ratio (HR) 18.9 Median follow-up (mos) 23.4 P-III (N=624) (1L Locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with EGFR mutations) Aumolertinib + Chemotherapy (n=310) Aumolertinib Alone (n=314) Study Design • Aumolertinib plus chemotherapy significantly improves progression-free survival in EGFR-mutant NSCLC, setting a new treatment benchmark • The combination shows benefits across mutation types and brain metastases, expanding patient options • Despite higher side effects, treatment discontinuation remains low, indicating manageable safety • Aumolertinib could challenge current market leaders like osimertinib, especially in China and potentially globally Implications Aumolertinib + Chemotherapy Aumolertinib Grade ≥3 AEs (%) 75.7 23.7 AEs leading to discontinuation (%) 3 1.3 Trial Location: China

BRIA-IMT: LATE-BREAKER P-III STUDY RESULTS Bria-IMT, a combination immunotherapy comprising the allogeneic whole-cell vaccine SV-BR-1-GM BRIA-ABC Bria-IMT regimen (Day -2 or -3 Cyclophosphamide 300mg/m2 Day 0 SV-BR-1-GM given intradermally divided into 4 inoculations Day 1-3 CPI infusion plus interferon administered intra-dermally within each SV-BR-1-GM inoculation site) + Retifanlimab vs TPC (N= 62) Bria-IMT With or Without CPI Treatment of Patients'/Physicians' Choice (TPC) Any HLA Match Median PFS (mos) 3.10 3.16 No HLA Match Median PFS (mos) 4.00 2.80 Hazard Ratio (HR) 0.77 2.226 p Value 0.59 0.6803 mPFS (mos) 3.67 Adverse events occurring in > 10% of patients (%) 27.4 25.8 24.2 20.9 17.7 17.7 17.7 16 16 14.5 14.5 12.9 12.9 P-III (Advanced MBC, failed all approved regimens) Bria-IMT Regimen + CPI (n=177) Treatment of Patients'/Phy sicians' Choice (n=177) Bria-IMT Regimen Alone (n=50) Study Design Interim Analysis at 144 events. If HR is 0.6, submit BLA. IF >0.6, continue to completion with HR target of 0.7 Final Analysis: PFS, CBR, OS Bria-IMT Regimen + CPI • DTH+ showed better PFS (4.47 vs 2.53 mos, p = 0.001) • Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) < 0.7 and ≥ 2.3 following the 1st treatment showed 3.07 mPFS (p = 0.02) • Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) < 1 showed better PFS (3.8 vs 2.4 mos, p = 0.04) • Baseline CAML count ≥ 5 showed higher mPFS (3.7 vs 2.2 mos, p = 0.10) Prespecified subset analyses of PFS based on biomarker status • Positive P-III data and new biomarkers suggest their breast cancer therapy could see faster approval, attract investors, and gain a competitive edge in the market due to its safety and personalized approach Implications

KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab), an anti-programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) therapy KEYNOTE-689 KEYTRUDA: P-III STUDY RESULTS KEYTRUDA as neoadj followed by KEYTRUDA + SoC radiotherapy with or without cisplatin Adj SoC radiotherapy with or without cisplatin In CPS ≥10 population Risk of EFS events reduction (%) 34 - mEFS (mos) 59.7 26.9 mPR rate (%) 13.7 - In CPS ≥1 population Risk of EFS events reduction in CPS ≥1 population (%) 30 - mEFS in CPS ≥1 population (mos) 59.7 29.6 mPR rate (%) 9.8 - In ITT population Risk of EFS events reduction (%) 27 - mEFS in ITT population (mos) 51.8 30.4 mPR rate (%) 9.3 - Median follow-up (mos) 38.3 OS Not reached statistical significance at the time of this interim analysis Grade ≥3 TRAEs (%) 44.6 42.9 TRAEs leading to death (%) 1.1 0.3 Immune-mediated AEs of any grade (%) 43.2 (most commonly hypothyroidism: 24.7%) - P-III (N=714) (Treatment-naïve newly diagnosed, stage III or IVA resectable, locally advanced HNSCC) KEYTRUDA (200 mg IV Q3W for 2 cycles as neoadj followed by KEYTRUDA (200 mg IV Q3W for 15 cycles) + SoC radiotherapy + cisplatin (100 mg/m2IV Q3W for 3 cycles) as adj following surgery for high-risk pts or KEYTRUDA (200 mg IV Q3W for 15 cycles) + SoC radiotherapy as adj following surgery for low-risk pts No neoadj prior to surgery, followed by adj SoC radiotherapy with cisplatin (100 mg/m2IV Q3W for 3 cycles) as adj following surgery for high-risk pts or SoC radiotherapy as adj following surgery for low-risk pts Study Design • KEYTRUDA could become the new standard perioperative treatment for resectable head and neck cancer, improving EFS • Expands KEYTRUDA’s use into earlier-stage cancers, supporting revenue growth despite patent challenges • FDA priority review may speed approval and boost market share Implications sBLA for KEYTRUDA, supported by data from KEYNOTE-689, is under priority review by the FDA; (PDUFA date June 23, 2025)

KEY INSIGHTS FROM AACR 2025 Antibody Drug Conjugate (ADC) • Next-gen ADCs with novel payloads and targets are broadening indications and improving efficacy in GI, breast, and lung cancers. Example: Mabwell’s 7MW4911 (CDH17 targeting) shows early promise. Bispecific/Trispecific Antibodies • Multi-specific antibodies (e.g., PD-1 + IL-12) are overcoming resistance and enhancing immune engagement in solid tumors. Cell & Gene Therapies • Advances in CAR-T, NK, and TIL therapies are expanding to solid tumors, with improved engineering for potency and safety. Targeted Therapies: RAS & Beyond • KRAS inhibitors (e.g., zoldonrasib, RMC-9805) achieve >60% response in NSCLC, reflecting progress against undruggable targets. Early-Phase Clinical Breakthroughs • First-in-human data on HER2xCD3 bispecific, novel small molecules, and more-12+ new agents entering trials. AI in Oncology • AI models now match experts in risk prediction, trial design, and patient selection, accelerating discovery and precision care. Liquid Biopsy & ctDNA • ctDNA guides adjuvant therapy, detects minimal residual disease, and enables earlier, noninvasive monitoring of recurrence. Cancer Vaccines • Personalized vaccines (e.g., NeoAg-VAX) show immune activation in cold tumors like MSS mCRC and glioblastoma. Patient-Centric Innovation • Focus on survivorship, quality of life, and equitable access-bridging research and real-world patient benefit.
